#### A. Foundations (what Audio is)

**AA-1. Can audio lie? One corruptible family, nothing else.**
*Rule.* Audio has exactly one PERCEIVED family, `hal`, played only for the viewer the Perception Filter names, only on a Filter audio request, and only with an audible leak (AA-35). Every other family is TRUE: its cue exists if and only if the published true fact exists, at the true place, with the true parameters, at every sanity stage and Filter state. The one-sentence answer is the Overview's: *audio can lie only through the hallucination family the Perception Filter requests for one viewer, every member of which carries an audible leak; the witness sounds, running-loop sounds, tell and breach audio, Horror's sounds, Suit and body cues, footsteps and foley, the human voice and the P1 proximity cue never lie, are never suppressed, and are identical at every sanity stage.* Audio corruption is inside the Filter's write set as audio requests, under the same rules as a visual lie (SN-25; PF-20). The voice channel (VS-B) and the P1 proximity cue are TRUE and are never altered, faked, silenced or delayed by any Filter or sanity state. At MVP the family has one sound signature, the class-(b) reading-lie signature, realised under the Filter's two MVP ids (AA-35); phantom movement (class a) is VS-A; class (c) adds no hallucinated sound (the P1 cue is true).
*Why.* HR-5 needs a sound signature on every lying reading; SN-25 authorises a hallucination family; `LSG:976` and `LSG:864` say phantom-entity audio is "in its own classes"; AT-17 forbids a false calm or phantom tell at any tier. "Audio never lies" contradicts HR-5 and SN-25; "audio lies anywhere off the consequence channel" breaks the tell and P3.
*Pillar.* P1, P4. *Decided by.* SN-25; PF-20; HR-5 (`ART:976`); AT-17, AUD-7; `LSG:976`; `IDX:41` (the voice channel is never faked).

**AA-2. The truth-class table (required artefact).** Exactly one row is PERCEIVED.

| Family (token) | Trigger fact | Published source | Truth | Tier | Captionable | Slice |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Witness (`wit`) | a live descriptor with `acoustic != NONE` and `medium != NONE` | Graph descriptor fields, `failures(filter)` | TRUE | 1 | Y | MVP |
| Graph alarm-class annunciator (`ann`, klaxon timbre; bus Witness) | a descriptor with `alarm_eligible` | Graph descriptor field | TRUE | 1 | Y | MVP |
| Running (`run`) | node `state` OK or DEGRADED with `served_pm` > 0; INTEGRITY compartment pressurised (the INTEGRITY room tone is `run`, AA-26) | Graph `node(id)`, `loop_component()`, `N/` `L/` keys | TRUE | 1 | Y | MVP |
| Footsteps (`foot`) | Controller gait class WALK, RUN or CARRY plus the odometer cycle position crossing a foot-contact frame (PC-11) | Controller odometer, gait | TRUE | 1 | Y (own-action foley, CX-A7) | MVP |
| Suit body (`suit`) | Suit cue state fields | Suit read view | TRUE | 1 | Y | MVP |
| Tell (`attn`): onset, beats, bed stems, release, breach entry, alarm pulses, subside | `attention.view` deltas | `attention.view` | TRUE | 2 | **N** | MVP |
| Tell (`attn`): positional hull-stress layer | `phase == TELL`, `tier >= 2`, `locus_section_id` | `attention.view` | TRUE | 3 | **N** | MVP |
| Tell (`attn`): pre-tell hull-settling creaks | `phase == CALM`, quantised cue step >= 1 | `attention.view` via `ambient_cue_step` | TRUE | 4 | **N** | MVP |
| Horror (`hor`): strike, REACH resolve | `strike_T`, `reach_end_T` | `horror.view` | TRUE | 2 | **N** | MVP |
| Horror (`hor`): floor-borne creep, ingress/egress creak | `pos_px`, ingress/egress events | `horror.view` | TRUE | 3 | **N** | MVP |
| Interaction (`ia`) | `channel_view` transitions, `result_seq` | Interaction | TRUE | 4 | Y (three terminals, `IA:979`) | MVP |
| Assembly (`asm`) | `last_result` with `outcome_cue_gate`; seam-cut TOOL loop | Assembly | TRUE | 4 | Y | MVP |
| Body and pod (`body`, `pod`) | `BODY_*`, `POD_*`, `BERTHED`, `UNBERTHED` events; the BERTHING state read (berth bed) | Body, Web Map | TRUE | 4 | Y | berth bed and berth cues MVP; `BODY_*` and the pod leg bed wired MVP, assets VS |
| P1 proximity cue (`p1c`) | another seat's `sanity_view.tell_on` | `sanity_view` | TRUE | 3 | **N** | contract MVP, live VS-B |
| Voice (`vox`) | human speech | Chat/Voice (VS-B) | TRUE | outside the world mix | n/a | VS-B |
| Ambience (`amb`) | static room tone | static data | TRUE | 4 | N | MVP minimal |
| UI (`ui`) | HUD and menu events (including `UI_INSTRUMENT_CARD_OPEN` / `UI_INSTRUMENT_CARD_CLOSE` and `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | HUD, designed (hud-and-suit-layer.md); Instruments (the card events); Chart Table, Web Map and Menus (`UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED`, CT-3, ASK-CT-20) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | TRUE | outside the world mix | Y | MVP minimal |
| Music (`mus`) | none at MVP | none | TRUE | 5 | n/a | VS/Alpha |
| **Hallucination (`hal`)** | a Filter audio request with SOUND in the lie's leak modes | Filter request *(designed; re-checked at the X-6 scan)* | **PERCEIVED** | 3, voice guaranteed (AA-12) | **N** | MVP one signature |

*Why.* A single table makes the lint (AA-6) a lookup and the "can audio lie?" answer checkable by anyone. Hidden real entities keep their sounds (`CON:243`, `SN:306`): a hallucination that hides a horror's body never silences its creep. *Pillar.* P1, P4. *Decided by.* SN-27; AT-17; the routed truth-class requirement.

**AA-3. Audio is a PRESENTATION subscriber that owns no sim state, and every rule is a pure function of published state.**
*Rule.* Audio registers no hook, no state block, no mutator, no command and no `push_stimulus` (KRN H1, H4, `KRN:125`); it persists nothing (cues are transitions-only, `AT:269`); it reads `SIM` and `PERCEPTION_OUT` views and writes audio nodes only (`KRN:110`); the P5 handlers and the frame poll hold no write capability *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (GDScript has no run-time "writes disabled" mode, so none is claimed: a snapshot test and a source lint prove it, AC-AA-84). Attention and the Graph read nothing of Audio: no audio symbol in their source, and muting any bus leaves `state_hash` unchanged (AUD-9; AC-AT-09). Audio never causes a tick, and pausing audio never pauses the sim (CR-11). Audio never reads `sanity.perception` (SN-23, CR-12): it consumes only what the Filter supplies. **Every cue is the output of one pure function**, `cue_requests(published_state, presentation_memory) -> [request]`, testable headless with a dummy audio driver; playing a request is the engine layer. A request carries (the `cue_request` record; registry: `cue_request`):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `cue_id` | an identity-table row (AA-6); never reused across families |
| `family`, `tier` | the truth class and M3 tier (AA-2, AA-11) |
| `kind` | `ONESHOT` or `SUSTAINED` (States and Transitions, cue kinds) |
| `anchor` | `{body_id, ship-local px}` or NONE (NONE = non-positional: the tell bed, the alarm pulses, UI) |
| `transmission` | AIRBORNE, STRUCTURE or NONE (AA-10) |
| `gain`, `pitch`, `rate` | source-side parameters before attenuation |
| `start_T`, `seek` | the requested start (sim `T`) and a late-start offset (restore only) |
| `listener_scope` | LOCAL, ALL_LIVING (the bed), ALL_EXCEPT_SOURCE (the P1 cue), OWNER_PRIVATE (hal requests, per seat; AA-46) |
| `leak_flags` | `hal` only; SOUND, copied from the Filter's request |

Floats are allowed in the presentation layer (it never feeds the sim, CR-11); *which* cues exist is exact (integers and published counters). -> ADR candidate: presentation-subscriber polling, the request record and the node-layer mapping.
*Why.* KRN CR-10, CR-11, CR-12; headless CI has no audio driver, so audibility is a manual test and cue selection must be automatic. *Pillar.* P1. *Decided by.* KRN H1/H4/H5, AUD-9, SN-23, `current-best-practices.md:181`.

**AA-4. Cue delivery: poll counters, edge-detect, one beat per poll, no catch-up.**
*Rule.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **One pipeline, two steps; only the second creates requests.** (1) The P5 notification handlers (CR-10) only *record*: each stores the latest published counters and dirty keys into the presentation memory's mailbox. A handler is idempotent (running it once per sim step of a catch-up frame leaves the same mailbox as running it once) and it creates no cue request, schedules nothing and calls no `play()`. (2) One **frame poll** per render frame, ordered after the frame's last sim step and notification and before the presenter's draw of that frame (a call-order guarantee, AA-13), reads the mailbox, classifies the net change and creates the requests. A fact published in a catch-up frame is therefore requested in that same frame and before the presenter draws, never once per sim step. The poll below is that frame poll: it compares published counters with last-seen values held in presentation memory (D.1): `(tell_epoch, tell_beat)` lexicographically, `phase`, `tier`, `tell_outcome`, `transition_seq` and `result_seq`, the `N/<id>`, `L/<loop>/<anchor>`, `C/<cid>`, `B/<cid>`, `F/<id>` dirty keys (Graph, LS-20) and `E/<id>` (Emitter, `EM:338`), `BODY_*` and `POD_*` events, and `horror.view` entry runs. A cue fires on a strictly greater pair, and the last-seen value is then set to the **observed** value whether or not a cue played (never `seen + 1`): at most one beat per poll, no catch-up burst after a hitch, pause or restore (AUD-3; AC-AT-115). A poll classifies the net change from `seen` to `now`; the D.1 rows are mutually exclusive on the published `(ph, e, b)`, so at most one event plays (ONSET, BEAT, RELEASE, BREACH_ENTER or SUBSIDE), and the intermediate transitions of a hitch are not played (D.1, E-AA-67, E-AA-68). The only time-dependent cues are those whose tick was already published (the REACH resolve, AA-28): the frame poll starts one when sim `T` has reached its published start tick and evaluates its position as a function of `T` (no timer exists, so pause freezes it by holding `T`). Timing is never taken from `_process` wall time. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Dirty keys wake discrete cues (a loop on or off); smooth values (`served_pm`, `intensity_pm`) are polled at render rate (`LSG:201`).
*Why.* AUD-1 forbids a timer in Audio. A `seen + 1` rule would replay skipped beats one per frame; a restore that left `seen` ahead of an earlier published epoch would drop the next real onset, which is a false calm. *Pillar.* P2, P3. *Decided by.* AUD-1, AUD-3; KRN CR-10; `audio.md` (timing from state).

**AA-5. Sustained cues versus one-shot cues; pause, restore, death.**
*Rule.* Cues are of two kinds (States and Transitions, cue kinds). **Sustained** cues (running loops, the INTEGRITY room tone, witness classes of live descriptors, Suit breath loops, the tell bed and its tier layers, the positional hull-stress layer, an in-progress seam-cut TOOL loop, an active lie's SOUND leak, the P1 loop, **and a REACH resolve whose `reach_end_T` is still in the future**) resume after a restore *from published state* at steady level with only a `DECLICK_TICKS` de-click and no attack transient; the exceptions are the tell bed, which fades in over `RESTORE_FADE_TICKS`, and an active lie's leak, which resumes at full leak level on the first frame (the Filter keeps no clean frame, PF-33). **One-shot** cues (onset, beat, release, breach entry, alarm pulse, subside, pre-tell creak, strike, interaction terminals, assembly outcome, `BODY_*`) **never replay** on a restore: the poll primes every last-seen value from the restored state and plays nothing (transitions only, AUD-6, AT-27). Pause holds sim `T`, so every sim-derived sound pauses and UI sounds continue. **Death plays no sound**; the death stub (`restore_reason DEATH_STUB`) is a restore like any other, and no content depends on `restore_reason` (SL-7, SL-21). Saving plays no sound. *(orchestrator ruling: the REACH resolve is SUSTAINED-with-seek on restore, as the systems-designer proposed: it is a pure function of a published future tick, so dropping it would silence a telegraph the player is owed; replaying a past strike is what is forbidden, and the strike stays one-shot. The sustained part is the non-percussive lead-in only, which ends at `reach_end_T` with no impact, so a restore that seeks into it asserts no strike (AA-28 b; checkpoint ruling 2026-10-26).)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Mechanism** *([UNV]: `docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/audio.md` carries no pause, envelope or voice-pool guidance beyond the pooling pattern; the shape below is the design intent to be checked at the first spike).* Pause is applied by the frame poll setting `stream_paused` on every world-family voice while the kernel state is PAUSED (UI and Voice voices are untouched, and `SceneTree.paused` is not used for audio, so UI sounds continue). **Every world-voice envelope is a pure function of sim `T` written in the frame poll** (`volume_db`, `pitch_scale`): the restore fade, release, tier crossfade, ducking, the slews, the leg and berth beds, the `hal` breathing and the REACH lead-in. **No `Tween`, `Timer` or wall-clock call drives a world voice** (lint L-15, AC-AA-73): a tween would keep running through a pause and would run on frame time, which is the timer AUD-1 forbids. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Envelope evaluation rules.** (a) An envelope is evaluated at the **tick-fractional** time `T + alpha`, where `alpha` is the Presenter's render-interpolation fraction of the fixed step (the accumulator remainder, which is a function of the step cadence and not a wall-clock read of audio; `[UNV]` that the Pipeline publishes it to Audio, otherwise `alpha` = 0 and the envelope steps at the tick rate), so a 2-tick de-click is not a staircase of 16.7 ms steps at render rates above the tick rate. (b) Every `volume_db` is clamped below at -80 dB (the engine floor; a faded voice is stopped, not left running at -80). (c) `DECLICK_TICKS` is at least `ceil(2 * p99 frame time / tick period)`, measured in the AC-AA-80 spike (at a 60 Hz tick and a 20 ms p99 that is 3 ticks), so a frame stall cannot make one step larger than the whole de-click; the default 2 is a placeholder until that measurement. (d) A frame that follows a stall longer than `STALL_RESYNC_MS` (100 `[PLACEHOLDER]`) writes every envelope at its value for the current `T` in one step and logs the DIAGNOSTIC `audio_stall_resync`. Whether a 2-tick de-click produces audible zipper noise is **not** settled: the engine probably ramps within its mix chunk `[UNV]`, and the real risks are frame stalls, tick quantisation and latency; the spike measures all three (AC-AA-81).
*Pillar.* P2, P4, P5. *Decided by.* run ruling R18, AT-27, AUD-6, SL-7, SL-21, PF-33.

**AA-6. The master identity table and the M6 lint.**
*Rule.* Audio owns one identity table of every family. Each asset carries exactly one family token in its name (`sfx_<token>_<context>_<name>_<variant>`) and each family is bound to exactly one bus. The build-time lint, run over `assets/data/audio/tell_audio.json` and the asset directory, fails if: (a) any asset carries two tokens or none; (b) any sound id appears under two tokens; (c) a `hal` asset is bound to a non-`hal` bus or a non-`hal` asset to the `hal` bus; (d) the `wit` token set is not exactly the eight non-NONE LS-14 classes {HISS, DRIP, HUM_DROP, CLANK, WIND, TICK, SIZZLE, CREAK} (the loop variant lives in the `<context>` slot and is not part of the class set, AA-26); (e) any `wit` id exists for NONE or for a WORN descriptor; (f) a `hal` asset carries energy outside the reserved leak signature profile (AA-35) or a non-`hal` asset carries it; (g) any `hal` id is not listed in the Filter's `FILTER_AUDIO_CLASSES`; (h) any `attn`, `hor`, `p1c` or `ann` asset shares a sound id, a source recording or a timbre tag with `wit`, `hal` or each other (so `ann` stays disjoint from `attn`: the klaxon and the breach pulse are two identities on one clock). **Ownership is split once, not shared:** the Filter owns the *id namespace* `FILTER_AUDIO_CLASSES` and the request semantics; Audio owns the assets, mix, bus, the master table and the lint. The `hal` rows cite the Filter's ids by reference; Audio never defines or renames one. This rule is the target that replaces Horror's dangling "AUD-13" and Attention's dangling "AUD-14" cites (CX-A5).
*Why.* M6, AC-HE-71, SN-25, PF-20 ("only if the Filter names the ids can a lint prove disjointness"). One table, one lint, no dual authority over an id. *Pillar.* P1, P3, P4. *Decided by.* M6; PF-20; SN-25; run rulings R4 and R26.

**AA-9. Listener and positional model.**
*Rule.* The listener is the local player's avatar position, never the camera, its lead or its zoom. Positional attenuation and panning are functions of world-px distance and are identical at every step of the integer zoom ladder (k in [1, k_auto+2]) and at every camera lead. Sources on a moving body stay attached to their ship-local anchors, composed each frame through `section_offset` and the body transform. Cue requests are pure functions of published state (AA-3). **Gain is always the manual D.9 value, written per voice as `volume_db` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)***: the built-in `AudioStreamPlayer2D` attenuation cannot express D.9 (a `NEAR_PX` plateau, a log-distance slope of `DIST_SLOPE_DB` per doubling beyond it (`DIST_SLOPE_RUN_DB` for a running loop's base timbre), door and hull terms) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the text still described the superseded linear dB-per-tile law)*, so if 2D players are used their built-in attenuation is disabled and only pan is left to the engine. The spike (OQ-AA-1, AC-AA-81) therefore compares **pan mechanisms only**: `AudioStreamPlayer2D` with an `AudioListener2D` on the avatar *([UNV] inside the 640x360 SubViewport)* against a manual pan, and the manual pan is the named fallback *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the fallback is the ordered arms B then C below, B being relocated 2D players, not the panner-bus pool first)* (-> ADR candidate). **Localisation is horizontal pan plus level**; the y position of a source is conveyed by level alone, and whether a vertical cue is added is the residual of the range ruling (OQ-AA-43; the ruling of OQ-AA-32 (b) did not add one, so until it does localisation is pan plus level). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The non-positional tell bed does not depend on the spike, which is a further reason the bed is contractual. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Spike preconditions and fallback arms** (all engine behaviour `[UNV]` until AC-AA-81 and AC-AA-6 record a result). *Preconditions the spike must assert, because each fails silently:* (1) the `AudioListener2D` on the avatar is the current listener inside the SubViewport (without a current listener the engine falls back to the camera, which would make pan a function of the camera lead and zoom, AA-9's first sentence); the test moves the camera lead and the zoom and requires the pan to stay unchanged; (2) every `AudioStreamPlayer2D`'s `max_distance` is set to at least 2 x `R_AUDIBLE_MAX_PX` (1218 px) so the engine's own cull can never remove a far witness or running loop that D.9 keeps audible (built-in attenuation is disabled but the distance cull is separate); (3) the frame-poll owner is one node with `process_mode` always, world voices are paused by `stream_paused` (AA-5), and looping is set on the imported stream, not on the player; (4) the project mix rate is the AA-44 value. *Pan arms, in the order they are tried:* **A** `AudioStreamPlayer2D` with the avatar listener; **B** (cheaper fallback, named by the Godot review) `AudioStreamPlayer2D` voices relocated each frame to a computed offset from the listener that reproduces the D.9 pan (`dx` clamped to `PAN_SPAN_TILES`), still one player per voice; **C** (last resort) a manual panner bus pool, about 32 buses for the voice pool, which is expensive and is shown buildable only if A and B fail. The earlier text named only the manual pan, whose cost (one panner bus per voice) was not shown to be affordable. 
*Pillar.* P2. *Decided by.* PIPE (the camera has no audio role, integer ladder); `AT:989`, `AT:1278`; HIGH [UNV] SubViewport listener; reflexion pattern 3.

**AA-10. Transmission through geometry: it attenuates, it never culls a witness, and an unknown door is open.**
*Rule.* Airborne sources are attenuated by distance and by the closed doors and hull boundaries between the listener's room (`room_at`) and the source's room (D.9). Where the Graph publishes a door's true opening state the attenuation follows it continuously (a half-open door softens less than a shut one); **until that read exists an unknown door state is treated as open**, never closed (`opening(edge_id)`, Layout's ask, CX-A4). Transmission attenuates; it never removes a `wit` source with `sev >= 1` that is inside its class audible radius (a per-class floor, `WIT_AUDIBLE_FLOOR_DB`). Structure-borne sources (the positional hull-stress layer, the seam-cut TOOL loop, Horror's ingress and egress creak, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* and the base timbre of a running loop, which also takes the shallower `DIST_SLOPE_RUN_DB`, D.7, D.9, D.19 R-g) ignore door penalties and take a reduced hull penalty; the tell bed is non-positional and exempt from all of it (AA-16) (engine note: no `Area2D` bus-override zones; see Engine feasibility notes).
*Why.* A guessed muffle that hides a real hiss is a suppression by default: it breaks P1 and the `LSG:1110` lint. The seam-cut loop is the far-side victim's tell (ASK AU1, `MSA:1071`). The constants and the formula are Formulas (D.9) and Tuning Knobs.
*Pillar.* P1, P2. *Decided by.* P1; `LSG:1110`; AUD-4; BS-4 (listening is a stance). *(orchestrator ruling: this reverses the brief's interim default "closed unless known", per ruling R10.)*

**AA-11. Mix priority tiers and ducking.**
*Rule.* Five tiers, Attention's M3 verbatim: **(1)** Graph consequence cues (witness and running) and the player's own footsteps; **(2)** tell beats and the breach alarm; **(3)** the positional hull-stress layer; **(4)** ambient and pre-tell cues; **(5)** music. This GDD places the families M3 does not name *without reordering it*: Suit body cues are tier 1 (consequence channel, `SE:1222`); the tell bed stems and Horror's strike and REACH-resolve cues are tier 2 (the strike cue is the witness of strike one, `HE:1285`); Horror's creep and ingress/egress creak, the `hal` leak and the P1 cue are tier 3; foley, interaction, assembly, body events and ambience are tier 4; UI and Voice sit outside the world mix. **Ducking:** a tier-4 or lower-importance bed (ambience, the TOOL channel loops **except the seam-cut TOOL loop, which is never ducked**, the pod leg bed, the berth bed) ducks under a tier-2 impulse cue (a beat, a strike, a breach pulse) by `DUCK_DB` for a short envelope. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Ducking is applied per voice** (the frame poll writes the victim's `volume_db`, D.18), never by a bus effect or a sidechain: the Foley bus carries tier-1 footfalls beside tier-4 interaction and assembly cues, so a bus-level duck would duck a tier-1 cue (L-8). **The tell family, the `hal` leak, Horror's cues, the seam-cut TOOL loop (the far-side victim's tell, AA-33) and every tier-1 cue are never ducked**, and **no compressor, limiter or sidechain may attenuate a tier-1 cue**. Beats never duck under music (music is empty at MVP). The alarm family's duty is capped at `ALARM_DUTY_MAX_PM` of each sweep (D.2). Hallucination cues never duck, delay or mask a true cue (AA-37). *(orchestrator ruling: ducking reaches tiers >= 4 only, the systems-designer's scope, not the audio-director's wider "beds including the hull-stress layer"; a duck on the positional hull-stress layer, a Horror creep or a lie's leak would mask a truth or leak channel, and M3's "beds" is read as the tier-4 beds.)*
*Pillar.* P1, P2. *Decided by.* M3, HE-37, SE-29, SN L-A.

**AA-12. Voice budget, reserved impulse voices, stealing order.**
*Rule.* A fixed pool of `VOICE_POOL_SIZE` voices (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 32, `[UNV]`). `RESERVED_TELL_IMPULSE_VOICES` of them (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was 2; see below)*; floor 1, which is M5's literal "one reserved voice") are reserved for tell and alarm one-shots (onset carrying beat 0, beats, breach entry, alarm pulses, release, subside) and are never lent to another family. The reserve is `ceil(BEAT_TAIL_MAX_TICKS / BEAT_MIN_GAP_TICKS) + 1` = 3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier formula gave 2 and omitted the "+ 1" that this very sentence named)* because a beat's tail can outlast the next beat's start (two live beat tails at the 30-tick floor of the gap) **and** the breach-entry event overlaps the last beat's tail (D.10); every tail is bounded by lint L-14, which now covers the onset and every beat asset (at most `BEAT_TAIL_MAX_TICKS`), so the count cannot grow with an asset; M5's "one" is therefore read as a floor. The **tell bed is a persistent looping stream outside the pool (pool-exempt)**, so a full pool can never drop the bed (CX-A12); the **INTEGRITY room tone** is likewise one pool-exempt stream per listener, so a consequence-channel sound cannot be stolen (D.7, D.10). When no voice is free, a request steals from the playing voice of the highest tier number that is strictly lower in importance than the request, then the quietest at the listener, then the oldest; a request that finds no victim is dropped; tier-1 and tier-2 voices are never stolen by tier-3-to-5 requests; the tell family and `hal` voices are PROTECTED, and **the seam-cut TOOL loop is not stealable by tier >= 4 requests**. **A presented lie's SOUND leak is never stolen while the number of lies is within `LIES_MAX`** (Sanity's registered constant, cited by name): a lie that is visually presented but has lost its leak would be unfalsifiable by sound. Pre-tell creaks and foley drop first. A witness is never culled for voice count while any tier >= 2 voice is stealable; a tier-1 steal raises a DIAGNOSTIC counter whose non-zero value in a CI soak is a bug (the audibility cull must trigger before the count cull). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `WIT_VOICE_CAP` counts voices, each descriptor costing `V_wit` (D.10); among tier-1 voices the victim is the lowest `sev`, then the quietest at the listener; every drop raises a named DIAGNOSTIC; the pool is sized from a measured worst-case scene, not from the sum of the caps. *(orchestrator ruling: `VOICE_POOL_SIZE` stays 32 `[UNV]` as ruling R19 fixed it; the systems-designer's derivation (plausible worst-case demand 37, tiers 1 to 3 alone about 31) is carried to Formulas D.10 as the reason the range is 32 to 64 and to OQ-AA-9 as a recommendation of 48. It is not written as the value. `RESERVED_TELL_IMPULSE_VOICES` 2 is an addition to run ruling R19's list, a refinement of M5 confirmed at the 2026-10-26 checkpoint (OQ-AA-8 closed).)*
*Pillar.* P2, P4. *Decided by.* M3, M5; `LIES_MAX`; routed thread T6.

**AA-13. Audio first: by construction, not by latency.**
*Rule.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* "Audio no later than visual" (HR-9, AUD-2, AC-AT-24) is a **call-order guarantee plus a measured offset budget**, never an absolute latency. (a) *Call order:* the request for a fact is created, and the engine `play()` is called, in the frame poll (AA-4) of the frame in which the fact's notification arrived, and that poll is ordered before the presenter's draw of the same frame. Beat 0 is published in the `attention.step` run that enters TELL, and the presenter draws nothing for that epoch before it. `HE:1285`'s "strike_T to the positional strike cue starting within 1 tick (17 ms)" is the same ordering guarantee (the strike request is created in the frame poll of the frame whose notification published `strike_T`, positioned to start at `strike_T`; a catch-up frame can carry the fact later than one tick of wall time, so the guarantee is the order and the audible offset is the budget, OQ-AA-37). (b) *Offset budget:* the engine cannot observe the delay from `play()` to the DAC (device buffer, the Windows audio stack), so no rule states an absolute figure. The measured quantity is the **audio-versus-screen delta** of a cue and its visual twin on one clock (AC-AA-6: a loopback capture of the audio output beside a capture of the screen). An optional constant `AUDIO_LEAD_MS` (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 0, range 0 to 100) is the hold a presenter may apply uniformly to all its visual twins so that the measured delta stays non-negative at p95 on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*; it is set only from that measurement, is global and never per cue (M-2), and its presenters are Attention's and Horror's, so it is a routed ask and not an edit here.
*Pillar.* P2. *Decided by.* AUD-2; `HE:1285`; KRN CR-10.

435	#### G. Accessibility, settings, data, bands and lints

437	**AA-41. Captions policy (policy now, implementation Alpha).**
438	*Rule.* **Captionable, with precise source-naming only:** `wit`, `ann` and `run` sounds, Suit body cues, foley (including the player's own run, provisionally as own-action foley because it names the player's gait, not the web's regard, CX-A7), the three terminal interaction sounds, UI. **Never captioned:** tell onset, beats, bed and release; the breach event and alarm cadence; pre-tell creaks; Horror sounds; the `hal` family; the P1 cue. Consistency check: because `hal` ids are disjoint from every captionable family, an uncaptioned `hal` sound never sits beside a captioned twin, so the caption set is not a lie oracle. A deaf or hard-of-hearing player's tell channel is **visual plus the opt-in haptic beat pulse** (AA-42, user ruling D51); no caption is added, the ruling having chosen the beat pulse, which carries the audio beat's information and nothing more, over a generic `[creaking]` caption. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* R-6: because audio can lie, the leak (AA-35) is the answer; precise source-naming of the captioned sounds is the other branch.
439	*Pillar.* P3, P4. *Decided by.* R-6 (`ART:962`), `AT:1223`, `HE:1342-1360`, OQ-AT-1.
440	
441	**AA-42. Tactile channel: none by default; two ruled exceptions (X10; D44, D51).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Default.* No rumble for the bed, the tell or Horror: a tell-synced rumble that is on for every player would be an Attention indicator under the standing user decision. *Exception (i), own body cues (D44, user ruling).* Haptics driven only by the player's own true body cues (the Suit's published breath, valve, shiver and stagger states) are not Attention indicators: they are the player's own consequence channel, keyed to Suit state and to nothing else. *Exception (ii), the beat pulse for the deaf or muted player in the dark (D51, user ruling).* An opt-in setting `haptic_beat_pulse`, **off by default**, plays one short controller pulse per published tell beat, on the same `(tell_epoch, tell_beat)` edge and under the same one-per-poll, no-catch-up, nothing-on-restore rules as the audio beat (AA-4, AA-15). It carries **the same information as the audio beat and nothing more**, which is why it is not an Attention indicator: fixed duration `HAPTIC_BEAT_MS` and strength `HAPTIC_BEAT_STRENGTH_PM`, never scaled by `tier`, tell progress, beat index or `level_pm`; the onset pulses once because the onset carries beat 0 (AA-14); no pulse for the bed, a tier step, the release, the breach entry, the alarm pulses, pre-tell creaks or Horror. The setting's UI is Alpha (Accessibility Settings, undesigned); `design/accessibility-requirements.md` is to be authored later with `/ux-design accessibility` and is not created here. OQ-AA-2 and OQ-AA-15 are resolved by this rule. *Pillar.* P3, P2. *Decided by.* `ART:954`, `AT:1331` (gains this exception: refresh owed, X-4), user rulings D44 and D51.
442	
443	**AA-43. Settings boundaries (rules now, UI Alpha).**
444	*Rule.* Per-group sliders exist for Music (`mus`), Ambience (`amb`), UI (`ui`) and Voice (`vox`). So no setting can strip the `hal` SOUND leak or the tell independently of the witness sounds. No setting lowers the tell bed below its margin relative to other world sounds (the margin is enforced relatively, D.6). Mono downmix keeps the bed. Reduce-flashing and reduce-motion never reduce audio (M1; FT E20, E21). 445	*Pillar.* P3, P4. *Decided by.* M1, M2, `ART:954` item 15; PF-15 ("never below two").

447	**AA-44. Data-driven assets and loudness.**
448	*Rule.* Every authored level, loudness (LU), radius, interval and class table lives in `assets/data/audio/tell_audio.json` (and sibling data files), never in code (coding standard). 451	**AA-45. The band plan and masking constraint (asset-spec constraints, `[PLACEHOLDER]` values).**
452	*Rule.* Masking is band-local, so the identity table is paired with a band plan that the asset spec enforces by an import-time tag: (a) the tell bed occupies a low structure-borne band plus an upper-partial edge layer so it survives laptop speakers (`[PLACEHOLDER]` about 30 to 120 Hz and 200 to 400 Hz); (b) the tell beat and onset carry a transient readable on a small speaker, so the beats carry the evidence when the bed is lost (AUD-5: each channel sufficient alone); (c) the POWER running hum's fundamental sits at or above `[PLACEHOLDER]` 160 Hz, outside the bed band (AA-26); (d) the Graph's HISS, WIND and SIZZLE are broadband noise well above the bed; TICK, CLANK and CREAK are mid-band impulses; (e) the `hal` fringe partial occupies a narrow reserved mid band (`[PLACEHOLDER]` about 1200 to 1800 Hz) that **no other family may occupy** (AA-6 f) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: "occupy" is narrowband prominence, a tonal peak over the asset's own broadband floor, not energy; the broadband families (HISS, WIND, SIZZLE) carry some energy there by nature and are not breaches)*; (f) Horror's creep and strike overlap the bed band by design and are accepted because they are positional and shorter, and the bed holds its margin against them as a non-tell sound. 466	
467	Audio owns **no sim state** and persists nothing. Audio itself causes no transition in any system.
468	
469	#### S1. Cue kinds, and what each does at restore, pause and death
470	
471	| Cue kind | Members | Trigger edge | On restore | On pause | On death stub | De-click / fade |
472	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
473	| Sustained, steady | `run` loops, the INTEGRITY room tone, `wit` classes of live descriptors, `suit` breath loops, an in-progress seam-cut TOOL loop, the `p1c` loop (VS-B), the positional hull-stress layer | the state is present (`N/<id>` and `L/<loop>/<anchor>` keys for running loops; the descriptor set woken by `F/<id>` keys for `wit` classes; `B/<cid>` keys for the INTEGRITY room tone; `phase == TELL` with `tier >= 2`) | resume at steady level from published state | held with sim `T` | stop (nothing is published) | `DECLICK_TICKS` |
474	| Sustained, tell bed | the `attn` bed and its tier stems | `phase == TELL` | **fade in over `RESTORE_FADE_TICKS`**; beats resume at the next published beat | held | stop | `RESTORE_FADE_TICKS` |
475	| Sustained, lie | the `hal` SOUND leak | an active Filter request (ON or LEVEL) | resume with the lie at full leak level on the first frame | held | stop | `DECLICK_TICKS` only |
476	| Sustained, scheduled | the REACH resolve while `reach_end_T` is in the future | a published `reach_end_T` | start with `seek` if inside the lead-in; the lead-in ends at `reach_end_T`; no impact without `strike_T` | frozen (it counts sim `T`) | stop | `DECLICK_TICKS` |
477	| One-shot | onset, beat, release, breach entry, alarm pulse, subside, pre-tell creak, strike, ingress/egress creak, `ia_*` terminals, assembly outcome, `BODY_*`, `POD_*` | a strictly greater counter or a new event | **never replays**; the poll primes last-seen values | held | no sound | n/a |

480	#### S2. The `attn` cue machine, as consumed from `attention.view`
481	
482	Attention owns the phases, timings and outcomes; this table lists only what Audio does on each *observed* delta. Audio reads `phase`, never `breach_phase` (AC-AT-67).
483	
484	| From (observed `phase`) | To | Observed delta | Audio action | Voice | Who causes it |
485	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
486	| CALM | CALM | quantised cue step change (`ambient_cue_step`) | the next creak predicate uses `CREAK_MEAN_TICKS[step]` and `CREAK_MIN_GAP_TICKS[step]` (AA-22) | pool, tier 4 | `attention.step` (level crossing a band edge) |

489	| TELL | TELL | `tier` increases | crossfade to the next bed layer over `TIER_XFADE_TICKS`; add the positional hull-stress layer at tier 2 | bed stream / pool tier 3 | `attention.step` (`TIER2_TICKS`, `TIER3_TICKS`, on the escalation clock that freezes while `L < theta_HOLD`; no tier change while frozen, and a tier never falls inside a TELL) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
490	| TELL | CALM | `tell_outcome == ABORTED` | beats stop; the bed decays over `RELEASE_TICKS`; the release cue | reserved impulse voice | the player's restraint, through Attention (`ABORT_HOLD_TICKS`) |

492	| BREACH | BREACH | the alarm clock reaches a pulse start (D.2) and the D.2 precedence rule admits it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | one alarm pulse, at most `ALARM_DUTY_MAX_PM` of the sweep | reserved impulse voice | the tick grid (a pure function of `T`, `breach_enter_T`, the listener's body) |

494	| SUBSIDING | CALM | `phase == CALM` | **nothing** (never an all-clear) | none | `attention.step` |
495	| CALM | BREACH | a hitch skipped TELL | breach entry as above; no stale beat, no onset | reserved impulse voice | `attention.step` |
496	| TELL | SUBSIDING, or CALM with `tell_outcome != ABORTED` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | a hitch (or a published jump) that skipped BREACH; no classifier row matches | no event and no cue; the sustained-state rule (D.1) fades the bed out over `BED_END_TICKS`; nothing is an all-clear | the bed stream only | `attention.step` |

502	|---|---|---|---|---|

504	| FALLBACK | at a pulse boundary: otherwise (derelict, `NOT_LIVE` home-ship, beacon absent or not yet commanded) | at a pulse boundary: ALIGNED conditions true | pulses at `(T - breach_enter_T) mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0` | the listener's body, the Emitter |

510	| State | Entry (Filter request) | Audio action | Exit | Who causes it |
511	|---|---|---|---|---|

513	| ONSET | ON on the first ACTIVE frame (`lie_tau = 0`) | the SOUND leak starts at once, no later than the glide becomes visible | `lie_tau >=` the arrival time | the Filter (PF-12, PF-15) |
514	| HOLD | the glide has arrived | the leak is sustained at the D.15 level with the per-lie breathing (`T_s` 4 to 6 s, trough `SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM`) from the ON *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, delegated ruling R8 under G1)* | the entry leaves `sanity.perception` | the Filter |
515	| RETURN | the entry left `sanity.perception` (expired, debunked or invalidated: indistinguishable) | the level follows the remaining discrepancy, with the over-reaching tail; never below the ACTIVE minimum before CLEAR; **no sting, no verdict, no relief cue** | the discrepancy is below the Filter's threshold, then OFF | the Filter (PF-12, PF-14) |
516	| restore | the post-restore notification | resume in whatever state the Filter reports from the first frame (no clean frame); the re-issued ON carries the lie's restore-exact `(T_s, floor)`; the breath restarts at its peak *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, delegated ruling R8 under G1)* | as above | Save/Load, the Filter |

518	A lie with no SOUND mode in force has no request, so no machine instance exists for it. A stage change never ends a lie (SN-16) and so never ends this machine.

521	
522	| State | Entry | Exit | Behaviour |
523	|---|---|---|---|
524	| ABSENT | `phase != TELL` and no release in progress | `phase == TELL` | no bed |
525	| RUNNING (tier 1/2/3) | onset; restore into TELL (with the `RESTORE_FADE_TICKS` fade) | tier step (layer crossfade) or TELL exit | base bed; layers added at tiers 2 and 3; unaffected by zoom, camera, room, transit, reduce-flashing |

*Rule.* Masking is band-local, so the identity table is paired with a band plan that the asset spec enforces by an import-time tag: (a) the tell bed occupies a low structure-borne band plus an upper-partial edge layer so it survives laptop speakers (`[PLACEHOLDER]` about 30 to 120 Hz and 200 to 400 Hz); (b) the tell beat and onset carry a transient readable on a small speaker, so the beats carry the evidence when the bed is lost (AUD-5: each channel sufficient alone); (c) the POWER running hum's fundamental sits at or above `[PLACEHOLDER]` 160 Hz, outside the bed band (AA-26); (d) the Graph's HISS, WIND and SIZZLE are broadband noise well above the bed; TICK, CLANK and CREAK are mid-band impulses; (e) the `hal` fringe partial occupies a narrow reserved mid band (`[PLACEHOLDER]` about 1200 to 1800 Hz) that **no other family may occupy** (AA-6 f) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: "occupy" is narrowband prominence, a tonal peak over the asset's own broadband floor, not energy; the broadband families (HISS, WIND, SIZZLE) carry some energy there by nature and are not breaches)*; (f) Horror's creep and strike overlap the bed band by design and are accepted because they are positional and shorter, and the bed holds its margin against them as a non-tell sound. Two families may share a primary band only if their temporal envelopes differ (impulse versus sustained). The lint stores each asset's spectral centroid and 80-per-cent-energy band and enforces `family -> allowed band`; **MVP default: the tag-only lint plus the blind tests (AC-AA-28, AC-AA-58); the spectral-centroid and band lint is a Vertical Slice upgrade** (CD-GDD-ALIGN, OQ-AA-5), adopted when the spike proves it feasible and not before.
*Pillar.* P2, P4. *Decided by.* M2, M6, run ruling R2; the systems-designer's band-plan risk (small speakers, bed band overlap).

**AA-46. Per-listener scope and co-op addressing `(provisional — Co-op Session undesigned)`.**
*Rule.* Every request carries a `listener_scope`: the tell bed is addressed to **ALL_LIVING** players (AT-15) and is the same at every client; positional layers are per listener; `hal` requests are `OWNER_PRIVATE` per seat; the P1 cue is ALL_EXCEPT_SOURCE; true sounds are identical on every client so "do you hear that too?" is a valid cross-check. A dead listener (VS-B) is addressed no bed. In the solo MVP there is one listener. Listener context (home-ship body, derelict, a pod in transit, a `NOT_LIVE` home-ship) changes only the alarm clock reference (AA-20), the door penalties (AA-10) and the pod leg bed (AA-33); the tell bed, the beats, the witness classes and the `hal` rules are identical in every context.
*Pillar.* P1, P2. *Decided by.* AT-15, SN-26.

**AA-47. Source lints (all build-breaking; each is a named acceptance criterion in part 2).**
*Rule.* L-1: no symbol `sanity.perception`, `tell_remaining`, `tell_progress_pm` or `breach_phase` in the audio source; `sanity_view` is read only by the P1-cue module. L-2: `level_pm` appears only as the argument of `ambient_cue_step`; no continuous audio parameter references it. L-3: only `hal` assets carry the `leak` tag; no other family's asset uses a `FILTER_AUDIO_CLASSES` id. L-4: asset tag families are pairwise disjoint (M6) and the `hal` fringe band is occupied by `hal` only. L-5: no code path lets a `hal` request modify, delay, duck or remove a request of another family. L-6: `ann` assets are reachable only from a descriptor with `alarm_eligible`; `attn` breach-entry and pulse assets only from the `attention.view` BREACH path; both run on the shared alarm grid (Graph LS-13 (d)) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. L-7: no request is generated for a descriptor with `medium == NONE` (WORN). L-8: no compressor, limiter or sidechain targets a tier-1 bus (M3), and there is no Master clip guard either: the D.19 peak relation (R-e) and the `master_peak_warn` DIAGNOSTIC replace it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. L-9: `release_cue_relation` is true at data load. L-10: every pre-tell asset tag differs from every beat asset tag, and the berth bed's hull-strain timbre tag differs from every `attn` tag (beat, bed, tier stem, pre-tell, breach entry, pulse). L-11: the M4 and M2 proxies hold for the asset set (an offline computation). L-12: no symbol of `AudioServer`, `AudioStreamPlayer*` or a bus in Attention's source (AUD-9, owned by Attention). L-13: no request path silences a `medium != NONE`, `sev >= 1` descriptor whose mode has no Graph-defined `intensity_pm`, or a SEAL_STRAIN in its HEAT/TICK branch (`LSG:649`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* L-14: every `ann` asset and every `attn` grid-pulse asset, tail included, is at most `W` ticks, and the breach-entry (pulse 0) asset, tail included, is at most `BREACH_ENTRY_TAIL_MAX_TICKS`, which is below `ALARM_MIN_GAP_TICKS` (D.2); *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* and the onset (which carries beat 0) and every beat asset, tail included, is at most `BEAT_TAIL_MAX_TICKS`, and every Horror strike and REACH-resolve asset is bounded the same way (the reserve sizing of D.10 depends on these tails). L-15: no `Tween`, `Timer`, `create_tween` or wall-clock call drives a world voice (AA-5). **Formula ids this section names** (written in Formulas, D.1 to D.20): D.1 cue dedupe and the per-poll classifier · D.2 alarm pulse phase, duty and minimum gap · D.3 release relation and bed release · D.4 restore bed fade · D.5 breach-entry loudness bound · D.6 bed audibility margin · D.7 running-timbre mapping · D.8 witness level and rate · D.9 room-graph transmission · D.10 voice allocation, reserve sizing and stealing order · D.11 REACH resolve scheduling · D.12 `outcome_cue_gate` usage · D.13 pre-tell creak predicate · D.14 footfall cadence and gait loudness · D.15 `hal` level and breathing · D.16 hull anchor derivation · D.17 pod leg bed envelope · D.18 ducking · D.19 audibility under masking and the peak budget *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* · D.20 annunciator step-down under sustained eligibility *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.

### States and Transitions

Audio owns **no sim state** and persists nothing. The machines below are *per-listener presentation memory*, rebuilt from published state after any restore; every transition is caused by a **change in a published fact** (never by a timer in Audio, AUD-1), and the "who may cause it" column names the owner of that fact. Audio itself causes no transition in any system.

#### S1. Cue kinds, and what each does at restore, pause and death

| Cue kind | Members | Trigger edge | On restore | On pause | On death stub | De-click / fade |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sustained, steady | `run` loops, the INTEGRITY room tone, `wit` classes of live descriptors, `suit` breath loops, an in-progress seam-cut TOOL loop, the `p1c` loop (VS-B), the positional hull-stress layer | the state is present (`N/<id>` and `L/<loop>/<anchor>` keys for running loops; the descriptor set woken by `F/<id>` keys for `wit` classes; `B/<cid>` keys for the INTEGRITY room tone; `phase == TELL` with `tier >= 2`) | resume at steady level from published state | held with sim `T` | stop (nothing is published) | `DECLICK_TICKS` |
| Sustained, tell bed | the `attn` bed and its tier stems | `phase == TELL` | **fade in over `RESTORE_FADE_TICKS`**; beats resume at the next published beat | held | stop | `RESTORE_FADE_TICKS` |
| Sustained, lie | the `hal` SOUND leak | an active Filter request (ON or LEVEL) | resume with the lie at full leak level on the first frame | held | stop | `DECLICK_TICKS` only |
| Sustained, scheduled | the REACH resolve while `reach_end_T` is in the future | a published `reach_end_T` | start with `seek` if inside the lead-in; the lead-in ends at `reach_end_T`; no impact without `strike_T` | frozen (it counts sim `T`) | stop | `DECLICK_TICKS` |
| One-shot | onset, beat, release, breach entry, alarm pulse, subside, pre-tell creak, strike, ingress/egress creak, `ia_*` terminals, assembly outcome, `BODY_*`, `POD_*` | a strictly greater counter or a new event | **never replays**; the poll primes last-seen values | held | no sound | n/a |
| UI | `ui` | a UI event | n/a | continues | n/a | n/a |

#### S2. The `attn` cue machine, as consumed from `attention.view`

Attention owns the phases, timings and outcomes; this table lists only what Audio does on each *observed* delta. Audio reads `phase`, never `breach_phase` (AC-AT-67).

| From (observed `phase`) | To | Observed delta | Audio action | Voice | Who causes it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CALM | CALM | quantised cue step change (`ambient_cue_step`) | the next creak predicate uses `CREAK_MEAN_TICKS[step]` and `CREAK_MIN_GAP_TICKS[step]` (AA-22) | pool, tier 4 | `attention.step` (level crossing a band edge) |
| CALM | TELL | new `tell_epoch`, `phase == TELL` | **onset (carries beat 0)**; the bed starts at tier layer 1; no new pre-tell creak starts | reserved impulse voice plus the bed stream | `attention.step` (Attention's level and arming) |
| TELL | TELL | `(tell_epoch, tell_beat)` strictly greater | **one beat** (at most one per poll) | reserved impulse voice | `attention.step` (`beat_schedule`) |
| TELL | TELL | `tier` increases | crossfade to the next bed layer over `TIER_XFADE_TICKS`; add the positional hull-stress layer at tier 2 | bed stream / pool tier 3 | `attention.step` (`TIER2_TICKS`, `TIER3_TICKS`, on the escalation clock that freezes while `L < theta_HOLD`; no tier change while frozen, and a tier never falls inside a TELL) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
| TELL | CALM | `tell_outcome == ABORTED` | beats stop; the bed decays over `RELEASE_TICKS`; the release cue | reserved impulse voice | the player's restraint, through Attention (`ABORT_HOLD_TICKS`) |
| TELL | BREACH | `phase == BREACH` | the bed stream fades out over `BED_END_TICKS` (no hard stop); the **breach-entry event is pulse 0**, with the bounded step (D.5); the alarm cadence begins *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | reserved impulse voice | `attention.step` (`breach_due_T`) |
| BREACH | BREACH | the alarm clock reaches a pulse start (D.2) and the D.2 precedence rule admits it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | one alarm pulse, at most `ALARM_DUTY_MAX_PM` of the sweep | reserved impulse voice | the tick grid (a pure function of `T`, `breach_enter_T`, the listener's body) |
| BREACH | SUBSIDING | `phase == SUBSIDING` | the alarm stops; one collapse; **no "danger over"** | reserved impulse voice | `attention.step` |
| SUBSIDING | CALM | `phase == CALM` | **nothing** (never an all-clear) | none | `attention.step` |
| CALM | BREACH | a hitch skipped TELL | breach entry as above; no stale beat, no onset | reserved impulse voice | `attention.step` |
| TELL | SUBSIDING, or CALM with `tell_outcome != ABORTED` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | a hitch (or a published jump) that skipped BREACH; no classifier row matches | no event and no cue; the sustained-state rule (D.1) fades the bed out over `BED_END_TICKS`; nothing is an all-clear | the bed stream only | `attention.step` |
| any | any (restore) | the post-restore notification | prime all last-seen values; no one-shot; the bed fades in if TELL; alarm pulses resume on the next grid tick if BREACH; nothing plays if CALM after ABORTED | the bed stream | Save/Load, Kernel |

#### S3. The alarm clock's branch (a small sub-machine inside BREACH)

| State | Entry | Exit | Behaviour | Who causes it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ALIGNED | at a pulse boundary: the debounced BEACON read is live (`BEACON_LIVE_HOLD_TICKS`) **and** the listener is on the home-ship's body *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | at a pulse boundary: either condition false | pulses at `T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0` | the Emitter (beacon commanded at T+1, off at SUBSIDING entry), the listener's body; the first choice is made at `breach_enter_T + BEACON_LIVE_HOLD_TICKS + 2`, so on the home ship pulse 0 is followed by an ALIGNED interval and never by a FALLBACK-then-switch |
| FALLBACK | at a pulse boundary: otherwise (derelict, `NOT_LIVE` home-ship, beacon absent or not yet commanded) | at a pulse boundary: ALIGNED conditions true | pulses at `(T - breach_enter_T) mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0` | the listener's body, the Emitter |

A pulse in either state follows the D.2 precedence rule *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: pulse 0 always emits; at most one `attn` and one `ann` start per tick (a same-tick pair stacks); every other start needs `ALARM_MIN_GAP_TICKS` against the latest alarm-family start on an earlier tick (`last_alarm_T`, shared with the Graph annunciator). The branch is re-evaluated only at a pulse boundary, and the debounced beacon read changes only after the raw read has differed for `BEACON_LIVE_HOLD_TICKS` ticks.

#### S4. The `hal` cue machine, as consumed from the Perception Filter `(designed; re-checked at the X-6 scan; states are Sanity's, mapped to sound by PF-12)`

| State | Entry (Filter request) | Audio action | Exit | Who causes it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NONE | no request for the ref | silent | an ON request | Sanity decides *whether, when, for whom*; the Filter emits the request |
| ONSET | ON on the first ACTIVE frame (`lie_tau = 0`) | the SOUND leak starts at once, no later than the glide becomes visible | `lie_tau >=` the arrival time | the Filter (PF-12, PF-15) |
| HOLD | the glide has arrived | the leak is sustained at the D.15 level with the per-lie breathing (`T_s` 4 to 6 s, trough `SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM`) from the ON *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, delegated ruling R8 under G1)* | the entry leaves `sanity.perception` | the Filter |
| RETURN | the entry left `sanity.perception` (expired, debunked or invalidated: indistinguishable) | the level follows the remaining discrepancy, with the over-reaching tail; never below the ACTIVE minimum before CLEAR; **no sting, no verdict, no relief cue** | the discrepancy is below the Filter's threshold, then OFF | the Filter (PF-12, PF-14) |
| restore | the post-restore notification | resume in whatever state the Filter reports from the first frame (no clean frame); the re-issued ON carries the lie's restore-exact `(T_s, floor)`; the breath restarts at its peak *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, delegated ruling R8 under G1)* | as above | Save/Load, the Filter |

A lie with no SOUND mode in force has no request, so no machine instance exists for it. A stage change never ends a lie (SN-16) and so never ends this machine.

#### S5. The tell bed's lifecycle (per listener)

| State | Entry | Exit | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| ABSENT | `phase != TELL` and no release in progress | `phase == TELL` | no bed |
| RUNNING (tier 1/2/3) | onset; restore into TELL (with the `RESTORE_FADE_TICKS` fade) | tier step (layer crossfade) or TELL exit | base bed; layers added at tiers 2 and 3; unaffected by zoom, camera, room, transit, reduce-flashing |
| RELEASING | TELL to CALM with ABORTED | `RELEASE_TICKS` elapsed | the level falls to silence by `BED_RELEASE_DEPTH_DB` over `RELEASE_TICKS`; a release cue sounds |
| ENDED | TELL to BREACH; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* or any observed `ph != TELL` with no RELEASE in progress (TELL to SUBSIDING, TELL to CALM with `out != ABORTED`; the D.1 sustained-state rule) | the stream has faded over `BED_END_TICKS` | the stream fades out from the entry tick and then stops; the breach-entry event's tail carries the transition when there is one, and otherwise the fade is silent *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

#### S6. Listener contexts (no change to cue content)

Listener on the home-ship's body, on a derelict, in a pod (LEG) or on a `NOT_LIVE` home-ship changes only (a) the alarm clock reference (S3), (b) the room-graph and door penalties (AA-10) and (c) the pod leg bed (AA-33). The tell bed, the beats, the witness classes and the `hal` rules are identical in every context (AA-46).

The fallback, were AUD-1 read as forbidding even a stateless recurrence, is one creak per step entry plus one per CALM-minute window; OQ-AA-7 was resolved at the 2026-10-26 checkpoint in favour of the predicate. 339	*Pillar.* P3. *Decided by.* AUD-1, AUD-8, AT-26, F-24 (`ambient_cue_step`).
340	
341	**AA-23. No false calm, no phantom tell, no held breath, no music before beat 0.**
342	*Rule.* The Filter and Sanity can never filter, delay, mute, double or synthesise tell or breach audio (AUD-7; AT-17). Adaptive music must not telegraph the tell earlier than beat 0 (there is no music at MVP, AA-40).
343	*Pillar.* P2, P3, P4. *Decided by.* AUD-7, AUD-8, `AT:1223`, AT-17.

*Pillar.* P2, P3. *Decided by.* V5, AUD-8, AT-26.

**AA-19. The abort: the web loses interest (release without reward).**
*Rule.* On TELL to CALM with `tell_outcome == ABORTED` the beats stop and the bed decays over `RELEASE_TICKS` (D.3), with a release cue whose spectral identity is distinct from subside's: an exhale or settling relaxation, with no sting, no reward chime and no "success" sound (relief without reward). The constraint is registered as one formula, `release_cue_relation`: `RELEASE_TICKS < ABORT_HOLD_TICKS` **and** `STRAND_RELEASE_TICKS == RELEASE_TICKS` (Attention owns `STRAND_RELEASE_TICKS`; equality is the requirement); a false relation at data load is a boot error. `TELL_REARM_TICKS` guarantees the release finishes long before any new onset. No beacon and no STRESS on an abort, so no breach cue. A restore into CALM with `tell_outcome == ABORTED` plays nothing (AA-5). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The release plays from whatever bed level the frozen escalation had reached (`L_bed0`, D.3): for a player who goes still before the escalation clock reaches `TIER2_TICKS` that is the tier-1 level, and no tier-2 layer and no hull-stress layer is heard first (X4; AC-AA-12, AC-AA-150).
*Why.* The player must hear the web lose interest or restraint is never learned (AUD-6, P3).
*Pillar.* P3, P2. *Decided by.* AUD-6; `AT:1150`, `AT:1258`; reflexion pattern 2.

**AA-20. Breach entry and the alarm cadence (the alarm-versus-`alarm_eligible` ruling, written into the live clause).**
*Rule.* On TELL to BREACH (or CALM to BREACH after a hitch that skipped TELL): (a) the **breach-entry event** plays on a reserved impulse voice at the entry notification, at `breach_enter_T`, and **is pulse 0 of the alarm cadence**, always emitted and exempt from the minimum gap by identity, not by tick order (d); its loudness step relative to the last tell beat is bounded by `BREACH_ENTRY_STEP_LU_MAX` (D.5): the tell precedes it, so it must not become a jump scare; (b) later pulses follow **one per `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS`** (M1), each sounding for at most `ALARM_DUTY_MAX_PM` of the sweep (D.2); (c) the pulse clock has two branches. **Aligned:** while `beacon_live` (`exists e in emitters() with e.kind == BEACON and e.body_id == the home-ship body and e.output_pm > 0`, EM-27, debounced by `BEACON_LIVE_HOLD_TICKS`, D.2) and the listener is on the home-ship's body, pulses start at the beam's sweep boundary, `T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0` (`beacon_aim` is a pure function of absolute `T`, so the beam returns to its authored phase exactly there, independent of `breach_enter_T`). **Fallback:** otherwise (listener on a derelict, home-ship `NOT_LIVE`, beacon absent or not yet commanded), pulses start at `(T - breach_enter_T) mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0`. Reduce-flashing never changes either branch; (d) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **one precedence rule, by identity (D.2)**: pulse 0 always emits and sets `last_alarm_T`; at most one `attn` pulse and at most one `ann` pulse may start on a tick (a same-tick pair is one rhythm with two stacked timbres, which is the normal case inside BREACH because both identities follow one `hit(T)`); every other pulse needs a gap of at least `ALARM_MIN_GAP_TICKS` (`BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS div 2`) against the latest alarm-family start on an *earlier* tick, so same-tick starters pass or fail together and pulse 0 is never suppressed by a gap against itself. The branch is re-evaluated **only at a pulse boundary** (the first choice is made at `breach_enter_T + BEACON_LIVE_HOLD_TICKS + 2`, after the beacon that is commanded at T+1 can be read), so a branch switch (the listener changes body mid-breach) or an aligned boundary landing soon after the entry event cannot double-sting inside a second, and the gap after a switch stays within `[ALARM_MIN_GAP_TICKS, 3 * ALARM_MIN_GAP_TICKS - 1]` ticks (64 to 191 at the registered sweep). **At entry and exit:** an `ann` pulse that started 1 to `ALARM_MIN_GAP_TICKS - 1` ticks before the entry finishes (no cut, as E-AA-17) and overlaps pulse 0 for at most `W - 1` ticks, and pulse 0 still emits; at BREACH exit the `ann` returns to the absolute grid and its first pulse obeys the same gap test, so its phase jumps at entry and at exit are each bounded to 64 to 191 ticks; (e) this event and cadence belong to the `attn` family, a tell-contract event that is **never "the first warning"** because a tell of at least `TELL_MIN_TICKS` precedes it by construction, so it is **exempt from the `alarm_eligible` gate** that governs the Graph's alarm-class annunciator (AA-27); the exemption is stated in the Graph (LS-13 (d), CX-A1 closed) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; (f) a lie never uses either identity (L-A, AUD-7); (g) audio carries the breach **alone** on a derelict (AUD-10), since the derelicts have no beacon. The tell bed fades out over `BED_END_TICKS` from the entry tick (no hard stop, so no click; D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the entry event's own tail (at most `BREACH_ENTRY_TAIL_MAX_TICKS`, lint L-14) carries the transition.
*Why.* Gating the siren on a `sev >= 3` descriptor would leave a breach with no such descriptor yet silent and, on a derelict with no beacon, inaudible: a P2 violation. A breach with no siren fails reduce-flashing players and derelict listeners. *(orchestrator ruling: the two specialist drafts agreed on the aligned phase `T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` and the fallback `(T - breach_enter_T) mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS`; the audio-director's draft let the first aligned pulse follow the entry event by 1 to 128 ticks, the systems-designer's added the minimum-gap suppression. The minimum-gap rule is adopted because M1 says "one pulse per sweep", which an entry event plus an aligned pulse a few ticks later would break. The aligned form needs no `beacon_phase` read, so the systems-designer's gap GAP-E1 does not arise; "beacon live" is read from the Emitter's `emitters()` view, `(provisional — Emitter read of a live BEACON, CX-A15)`.)*
*Pillar.* P2. *Decided by.* AT-18, M1, M4, AUD-10, `LSG:976`; `beacon_aim` (EM-16) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: dropped "wording refresh owed, CX-A1"; the Graph states the exemption in LS-13 (d))*.

**AA-21. Subside is not an all-clear.**
*Rule.* On BREACH to SUBSIDING the alarm cadence stops and **one short collapse** plays ("a short collapse, then silence", V10): no "danger over" cue, no relief sound. `phase == CALM` is **never** mapped to "all clear": no sound, music, ambience or mix change signals safety on entering CALM, and the Graph's failing-loop sounds (`wit`) carry the ongoing wrongness because STRESS can outlive SUBSIDING (`AT:1210`). Pre-tell creaks resume only by their own floor rule (AA-22). Audio reads `phase`, never `breach_phase`.
*Pillar.* P2, P3. *Decided by.* AUD-10, V10, `AT:1210`; AC-AT-67.

**AA-22. Pre-tell ambient creaks: stepped, floor-gated, in the listener's own section, never a meter.**
*Rule.* In `phase == CALM` only, ordinary hull-settling creaks (event ids distinct from tell beats, excluded from TellAudit and from the floor-window count) play at a density selected by the **quantised cue step** of Attention's `ambient_cue_step` (floor `AMBIENT_CUE_FLOOR_PM` 800 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*, `CUE_STEPS` 4, `CUE_HYST_PM` 25, `CUE_MARGIN_PM` 100; cited, never restated). Step 0 (below the floor) plays none. Steps 1 to `CUE_STEPS` use a four-row table of mean spacing and minimum gap (`CREAK_MEAN_TICKS` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 1800 / 1200 / 780 / 480 ticks, strictly decreasing, each step at least 1.3 times denser than the last; `CREAK_MIN_GAP_TICKS` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 600 / 480 / 360 / 240, each below its mean). **Recurrence is a stateless predicate of published state, never a countdown** (D.13): on each sim tick since the previous poll a creak is *eligible* when `phase == CALM`, the step is at least 1, `T - last_creak_T >= CREAK_MIN_GAP_TICKS[step]` and the shared integer presentation hash of `(T, HASH_SEED, step)` modulo `CREAK_MEAN_TICKS[step] - CREAK_MIN_GAP_TICKS[step]` is zero; at most one creak starts per poll (no catch-up), and evaluating every elapsed tick keeps the density independent of the frame rate. The scan span is **primed to the current `T` on a restore and on a resume from pause** (no backlog scan) and is capped at `CREAK_SCAN_MAX_TICKS` (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 60) ticks per poll (D.13), so a long hitch is a bounded loop, never a catch-up. The hash is the shared presentation hash (`HASH_SEED`, Attention, AT-28; the hash is shared with Lighting, LO-19), **never `rng_derive`** (a sim stream). **Position:** each creak is positional at a plate of **the listener's own section**, chosen by the hash, so a creak never points at the locus and is never louder, closer or pitched by step (a locus-anchored pre-tell creak would localise the future tell and make the step a distance meter by ear). A creak in flight at onset finishes. Pre-tell creaks stop at TELL entry and never play in BREACH or SUBSIDING. Four discrete densities, constant within a step: no continuous mapping of `level_pm` to any audible parameter, no pitched tone, no drone (AT-26). Creaks are a different timbre from tell beats (short, small, single-plate settle versus a deep structure-borne knock; lint L-10). `level_pm` appears in Audio only as the argument of `ambient_cue_step`. This rule is the pre-tell cue rule that replaces Attention's dangling "AUD-14" (CX-A5). *(orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's stateless-hash form is adopted over the audio-director's per-creak sampled delay, because AUD-1 says "never from a timer in Audio" and a sampled delay is a countdown; the audio-director's means (1440 / 960 / 660 / 480) are superseded. The fallback, were AUD-1 read as forbidding even a stateless recurrence, is one creak per step entry plus one per CALM-minute window; OQ-AA-7 was resolved at the 2026-10-26 checkpoint in favour of the predicate. Creaks are deliberately not suppressed in the ticks before a possible onset: a suppression would itself predict the tell.)*
*Why.* AUD-8, AT-26, F-24: a four-step table is the most the guard rail allows, and it is floor-gated so the step-1 cue sits above the lamp's walk-beam reading.
*Pillar.* P3. *Decided by.* AUD-1, AUD-8, AT-26, F-24 (`ambient_cue_step`).

**AA-23. No false calm, no phantom tell, no held breath, no music before beat 0.**
*Rule.* The Filter and Sanity can never filter, delay, mute, double or synthesise tell or breach audio (AUD-7; AT-17). No cue is suppressed during a real tell at any tier, stage or setting; no tell sound is ever played without a published tell. The "held breath" silence before breach is rejected (it would reduce evidence inside the floor window). A caption for tell beats is rejected (AA-41). Adaptive music must not telegraph the tell earlier than beat 0 (there is no music at MVP, AA-40).
*Pillar.* P2, P3, P4. *Decided by.* AUD-7, AUD-8, `AT:1223`, AT-17.

# TRs: Adaptive Audio & Tells (alias: audio)

Source: design/gdd/adaptive-audio-and-tells.md (Presentation layer, MVP, status Designed).

| Req ID | Requirement | Domain | GDD anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-audio-001 | Audio registers no hook, state block, mutator, command or `push_stimulus`; it is a `PRESENTATION` subscriber that reads `SIM` and `PERCEPTION_OUT` views and writes audio nodes only, and muting any bus leaves `state_hash` unchanged. | Core | AA-3, AUD-9, AC-AA-84 |
| TR-audio-002 | Audio persists nothing and is not hashed or replicated; its presentation memory (`(tell_epoch, tell_beat)`, `phase`, `transition_seq`, `result_seq`, `last_result.T`, shared `last_alarm_T`) is rebuilt from published state after any restore. | Save/Load | Overview data layer, AA-4, AA-5 |
| TR-audio-003 | Every cue is the output of one pure, headless-testable function `cue_requests(published_state, presentation_memory) -> [cue_request]`; the `cue_request` record carries cue_id, family, tier, kind, anchor, transmission, gain/pitch/rate, start_T, seek, listener_scope, leak_flags. | Core | AA-3 |
| TR-audio-004 | P5 notification handlers only record into a mailbox (idempotent, no cue creation or `play()`); one frame poll per render frame, ordered after the last sim step and before the presenter draw, classifies net change and creates all requests. | Threading/Timing | AA-4, AA-13 |
| TR-audio-005 | Cue dedupe uses last-seen counters set to the observed value (never seen+1): at most one beat per poll, no catch-up burst after hitch, pause or restore. | Threading/Timing | AA-4, AA-15, D.1 |
| TR-audio-006 | No timer exists in Audio: no `Tween`, `Timer`, `create_tween` or wall-clock call drives a world voice; all world-voice envelopes (`volume_db`, `pitch_scale`) are pure functions of sim `T` (+ render alpha) written in the frame poll, clamped at -80 dB. | Threading/Timing | AA-5, lint L-15, AC-AA-73 |
| TR-audio-007 | Pause sets `stream_paused` on all world voices while the kernel is PAUSED (UI and Voice voices continue, `SceneTree.paused` not used); audio never causes a tick and never pauses the sim. | Audio | AA-3, AA-5, E-AA-44 |
| TR-audio-008 | On restore, one-shot cues never replay and last-seen values are primed from restored state; sustained cues resume at steady level with `DECLICK_TICKS`, the tell bed fades in over `RESTORE_FADE_TICKS`, an active lie's leak resumes at full level on frame one, REACH lead-in resumes with `seek`. | Save/Load | AA-5, S1, E-AA-38..42 |
| TR-audio-009 | Death and save play no sound; `restore_reason` is never read by Audio. | Save/Load | AA-5, E-AA-45, SL-7 |
| TR-audio-010 | Exactly one audio family (`hal`) is PERCEIVED; all other families are true at every sanity stage, never suppressed, delayed or synthesised by the Filter or Sanity; audio never reads `sanity.perception`. | Core | AA-1, AA-2, AA-23, source lint L-1 |
| TR-audio-011 | A master identity table binds each asset (name `sfx_<token>_<context>_<name>_<variant>`) to exactly one family token and one bus; a build-time lint over `assets/data/audio/tell_audio.json` and the asset dir proves families disjoint and `hal` ids equal to the Filter's `FILTER_AUDIO_CLASSES`. | Data | AA-6, L-3, L-4 |
| TR-audio-012 | All levels, radii, intervals, loudness and class tables live in `assets/data/audio/tell_audio.json` (and sibling files), never in code; assets 48 kHz, mono for positional, OGG for loops/beds and sounds over `PCM_MAX_TICKS`, 16-bit PCM for short one-shots, all preloaded at boot. | Data | AA-44 |
| TR-audio-013 | Tell onset carries beat 0 on one reserved impulse voice, and each strictly-greater `(tell_epoch, tell_beat)` yields exactly one unpitched beat with no suppression before `breach_due_T`; audio starts no later than the visual twin by call order, not absolute latency. | Audio | AA-13, AA-14, AA-15 |
| TR-audio-014 | During `phase == TELL` a non-positional, pool-exempt structure-borne bed plays for every living player, never attenuated by distance, transmission, zoom, camera or room, at least `TELL_AUDIBILITY_MARGIN_DB` above the loudest concurrent non-tell bed per band. | Audio | AA-16, D.6 |
| TR-audio-015 | Tell tier layering is discrete (three tiers, `TIER_XFADE_TICKS` crossfade), no audible parameter varies continuously with `tell_elapsed` or `level_pm`, and `level_pm` is used only as the argument of `ambient_cue_step`; Audio reads `phase` never `breach_phase`. | Audio | AA-18, AA-22, L-1, L-2 |
| TR-audio-016 | Alarm clock: breach entry is pulse 0 (always emitted); later pulses one per `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` on ALIGNED or FALLBACK grid, at most one `attn` and one `ann` start per tick, gap >= `ALARM_MIN_GAP_TICKS` against `last_alarm_T`, branch re-evaluated only at pulse boundaries, duty capped by `ALARM_DUTY_MAX_PM`. | Threading/Timing | AA-20, S3, D.2 |
| TR-audio-017 | Pre-tell creaks are a stateless predicate over the shared presentation hash (`HASH_SEED`, never `rng_derive`), scan capped at `CREAK_SCAN_MAX_TICKS`, primed to current `T` on restore/resume, positioned in the listener's own section, four discrete density steps only in CALM. | Audio | AA-22, D.13 |
| TR-audio-018 | Abort plays a release cue and decays the bed over `RELEASE_TICKS`; `release_cue_relation` (`RELEASE_TICKS < ABORT_HOLD_TICKS` and `STRAND_RELEASE_TICKS == RELEASE_TICKS`) is a boot error if false; CALM and subside never map to an all-clear. | Audio | AA-19, AA-21, L-9 |
| TR-audio-019 | Witness (`wit`) cues exist iff a live Graph descriptor has `acoustic != NONE` and `medium != NONE`, positioned at the descriptor anchor with level/rate from `intensity_pm`/`sev`; eight classes only; the annunciator (`ann`) is reachable only from `alarm_eligible` descriptors. | Audio | AA-2, AA-6(d), AA-24, AA-27, L-6, L-7 |
| TR-audio-020 | Running loops (`run`) are read from `node()`/`loop_component()` and woken by `N/`, `L/`, `C/`, `B/`, `F/`, `E/` dirty keys; smooth values (`served_pm`, `intensity_pm`) are polled at render rate. | Audio | AA-4, AA-8, AA-26 |
| TR-audio-021 | Listener is the avatar position (never the camera, lead or zoom); gain is the manual D.9 value written per voice (built-in 2D attenuation disabled); transmission attenuates but never culls a `sev >= 1` witness; an unknown door state is treated as open. | Audio | AA-9, AA-10, D.9 |
| TR-audio-022 | Fixed voice pool (`VOICE_POOL_SIZE` 32 placeholder) with `RESERVED_TELL_IMPULSE_VOICES` (3) never lent out, pool-exempt tell bed and INTEGRITY room tone, deterministic stealing order (tier, quietest, oldest), tell and `hal` voices protected, named DIAGNOSTIC on any tier-1 steal. | Audio | AA-12, D.10 |
| TR-audio-023 | Mix priority is five tiers; ducking is applied per voice (not by bus effect/sidechain) only to tier >= 4 beds; no compressor, limiter or sidechain may attenuate a tier-1 cue; `hal` cues never duck, delay or mask a true cue. | Audio | AA-11, L-5, L-8, D.18 |
| TR-audio-024 | `hal` requests are `OWNER_PRIVATE` per seat, driven only by the Filter audio request `(viewer, ref/position, intent {ON, LEVEL(pm), OFF}, class)`, carry an audible leak with restore-exact `(T_s, floor)` breathing, and are never stolen while lies <= `LIES_MAX`. | Audio | AA-35, AA-46, S4, PF-20, D.15 |
| TR-audio-025 | Hull anchor of `locus_section_id` is derived by Audio from Layout's `plate_positions` composed with `section_offset` and the body transform (D.16); sources on moving bodies stay attached to ship-local anchors. | Physics | AA-9, AA-17, D.16 |
| TR-audio-026 | Cue delivery for Horror consumes `horror.view` (`strike_T`, `reach_end_T`, ingress/egress events); the REACH resolve is a sustained-with-seek cue evaluated as a function of `T`, and the strike cue never replays on restore. | Audio | AA-28, D.11, E-AA-42 |
| TR-audio-027 | Settings: one World slider covers all in-world families; no setting lowers the tell bed below its margin, strips a `hal` leak, sonifies Attention level, or is affected by reduce-flashing/reduce-motion; the only tactile exceptions are Suit own-body cues and the opt-in off-by-default `haptic_beat_pulse` (fixed duration/strength, same edge rules as the beat). | Input | AA-42, AA-43, L-18 |
| TR-audio-028 | Captions policy: `wit`, `ann`, `run`, `suit`, foley, three interaction terminals and UI are captionable; tell, breach/alarm, pre-tell creaks, Horror, `hal` and the P1 cue are never captioned. | UI | AA-41 |
| TR-audio-029 | Audio main-thread cost (poll, `cue_requests`, node updates) is at most `AUDIO_FRAME_BUDGET_US` (500 placeholder) at p95 on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK release export, with flat `OBJECT_COUNT` and `MEMORY_STATIC` after a 300-frame warm-up. | Performance | AC-AA-80, AA-3 |
| TR-audio-030 | Audio never reads Attention internals beyond the published `attention.view`; nothing in Attention or the Graph references Audio symbols (no `AudioServer`/`AudioStreamPlayer*`/bus in Attention source). | Core | AA-3, L-12, AUD-9 |

## Public surface

- Owned data and tables: master identity table (AA-6) and `assets/data/audio/tell_audio.json`; `cue_request` record (registry name `cue_request`); `cue_requests(published_state, presentation_memory)` pure function.
- Audio-owned constants: `RELEASE_TICKS`, `RESTORE_FADE_TICKS`, `ALARM_DUTY_MAX_PM`, `BREACH_ENTRY_STEP_LU_MAX`, `TELL_AUDIBILITY_MARGIN_DB`, `DECLICK_TICKS`, `BED_END_TICKS`, `TIER_XFADE_TICKS`, `TIER_STEP_DB`, `ALARM_MIN_GAP_TICKS`, `VOICE_POOL_SIZE`, `RESERVED_TELL_IMPULSE_VOICES`, `WIT_VOICE_CAP`, `WIT_MVP_ASSET_CAP`, `DUCK_DB`, `LEG_BED_FADE_TICKS`, `AUDIO_LEAD_MS`, `AUDIO_FRAME_BUDGET_US`, `CREAK_MEAN_TICKS`, `CREAK_MIN_GAP_TICKS`, `CREAK_SCAN_MAX_TICKS`, `DIST_SLOPE_DB`, `DIST_SLOPE_RUN_DB`, `NEAR_PX`, `R_AUDIBLE_MAX_PX`, `HAL_FLOOR_DB`, `HAPTIC_BEAT_MS`, `HAPTIC_BEAT_STRENGTH_PM`, `ANN_STEPDOWN_SWEEPS`.
- Formula `release_cue_relation`; formulas D.1 to D.20; source lints L-1 to L-19.
- UI-bus events adopted: `UI_INSTRUMENT_CARD_OPEN`, `UI_INSTRUMENT_CARD_CLOSE`, `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED`.
- Settings contract: `haptic_beat_pulse` (opt-in, off by default); per-group sliders Music/Ambience/UI/Voice/World.
- Bus tree: Tell, Witness, Run, Horror, Body, Foley, Hallucination, Ambience, UI, Voice, Music.
- Diagnostics: `voice_tier1_steal`, `audio_stall_resync`, `master_peak_warn`.
- Audio registers no hook, state block, mutator or command (it exposes no sim-facing API).

## Consumes

- Life-Support Graph (hard): descriptors (`acoustic`, `intensity_pm`, `sev`, `dir`, `alarm_eligible`, `cause`, `anchor`), `node(id)`, `edge(id)`, `loop_component()`, `failures(filter)`, `compartment(cid)`, dirty keys `N/ L/ C/ B/ F/`; ask `opening(edge_id)`.
- Attention System (hard): `attention.view` (`phase`, `tell_beat`, `tell_beat_T`, `tell_epoch`, `tier`, `tell_outcome`, `breach_enter_T`, `locus_section_id`, quantised `level_pm` via `ambient_cue_step`), `beat_schedule`, `tell_window_contract`, `HASH_SEED`.
- Horror Entities (hard): `horror.view` (state, `pos_px`, `section_id`, `locked_pt`, `reach_end_T`, `strike_T`, ingress/egress events).
